How much concrete do I need for a slab?

By the Metre team · Updated 26 Oct 2026 · 2 min read

Short answer

Volume = length × width × thickness. Example: 4 m × 3 m × 0.10 m = 1.2 m³. In US units, 13 ft × 10 ft × 4 in (0.333 ft) = 43.3 cu ft, which is 1.6 cubic yards. Add 5 to 10 % for waste and uneven ground. One cubic metre is 1.308 cubic yards, and one cubic yard is 27 cubic feet.

What you need

  • Length and width of the slab
  • The thickness you will pour
  • The yield printed on the bag, if you use bagged mix

Step by step

  1. Measure the length and width

    Measure the area to be poured. For an L-shape, split it into rectangles and add the volumes.

  2. Decide the thickness

    Common slabs for paths and patios are about 100 mm (4 in). Heavier loads need more, and your design or local rules decide the number.

  3. Convert to the same unit

    Work in metres (thickness in metres) or in feet (thickness in feet), then multiply: length × width × thickness.

  4. Add a waste allowance

    Add 5 to 10 % for spillage, uneven ground and a slightly deeper pour.

  5. Convert to what you will order

    Multiply cubic metres by 1.308 for cubic yards, or divide cubic feet by 27. For bagged mix, divide the volume by the yield printed on one bag.

Worked example (metric)

A 4 m × 3 m slab, 100 mm thick: 4 × 3 × 0.1 = 1.2 m³. With 10 % waste, order about 1.3 m³.

Worked example (US units)

A 13 ft × 10 ft slab, 4 in thick: 13 × 10 × 0.333 = 43.3 cu ft = 1.6 cu yd. With 10 % waste, order about 1.8 cu yd.

How accurate is this?

Concrete volumes are estimates. Ground that is not flat, edge forms and spillage change the amount, and concrete cannot be returned, so round up.

Measurements made with a phone are estimates. Before you cut, order or build, confirm critical dimensions with a physical tape.

Questions people ask

How do I calculate cubic metres of concrete?

Multiply length by width by thickness, all in metres. A 4 m × 3 m slab 0.1 m thick is 1.2 m³.

How do I convert m³ to cubic yards?

Multiply by 1.308. One cubic yard is 27 cubic feet.

How much extra should I order?

Add 5 to 10 % for waste and uneven ground.

How many bags of concrete for a 10 ft × 10 ft slab?

A 10 ft × 10 ft slab 4 in thick is 33.3 cu ft. An 80 lb (36 kg) bag of premixed concrete yields about 0.6 cu ft (0.017 m³), so you need about 56 bags, or around 60 with waste. Check the yield printed on your bag, because brands differ.
